History:
- Chief complaint: Recurrent severe headaches with “feeling hot,” plus systemic symptoms including tachycardia, shortness of breath, reduced appetite, weight loss, tingling in both arms, and decreased libido. Symptoms occur intermittently, mainly at work.
- Onset/duration/progression: Onset after changing jobs; episodes come and go, occurring during work (meetings, computer use). Headache typically frontal/around the head with nausea; dyspnea reported at desk; one instance described in an elevator. Timing is variable; no single triggering pattern identified.
- Context: 35-year-old male lawyer in London; high work-related stress (7–8/10). Sleep and other triggers not clearly described.
- Associated features: Light-to-moderate nausea with headaches; occasional breathing difficulty; palpitations (feels like heart beating fast); reduced appetite; unintentional weight loss (~5 lb); decreased libido.
- Past medical history: Hyperthyroidism; on thyroxine (levothyroxine); adherent to medication.
- Medications/allergies: Levothyroxine; dose/route/frequency not documented. Allergies: not reported.
- Social history: Drinks alcohol weekly (a couple of glasses of wine); does not smoke; no recreational drug use reported.

Past Medical History:
- Hyperthyroidism, on levothyroxine (dose/administration not documented).

Physical Examination:
- Not recorded in the transcript.

Impression:
- Primary: Suspected thyrotoxicosis/hyperthyroidism in the setting of known hyperthyroidism on levothyroxine therapy; symptom cluster (tachycardia, weight loss, heat intolerance, reduced appetite, libido change) after a job change.
- Differential considerations (consistent with transcript):
  - Migraine-type or tension-type headache with associated nausea.
  - Anxiety/panic syndrome with autonomic symptoms (tachycardia, dyspnea, paresthesias).
- Note: No imaging or lab results available yet.

Management Plan:
- Schedule and complete an in-person clinic evaluation to assess cardiac and pulmonary status.
- Obtain blood tests, including thyroid-related assessment (thyroxine level) and other baseline labs as part of standard evaluation.
- Review and potentially adjust levothyroxine dosing based on results.
- Follow-up: Clinic appointment arranged via the app; patient will be seen by another physician in the clinic and results reviewed to determine next steps.

Patient Summary:
- A 35-year-old man with known hyperthyroidism on thyroxine presents with episodic headaches, heat intolerance, tachycardia, dyspnea, weight loss, reduced appetite, arm tingling, and decreased libido, primarily at work. He will have an in-person clinic visit with thyroid function testing to clarify the cause and guide management.

Key Takeaways:
- Schedule an in-person clinic visit for a comprehensive exam (cardiac and pulmonary) and thyroid function testing.
- Thyroid function assessment is essential to evaluate for thyrotoxicosis/hyperthyroidism and possible levothyroxine dose adjustment.
- Monitor and report persistent or worsening symptoms; plan to review results after testing.

Next Steps:
- Complete in-clinic examination (heart and lungs) and order thyroid-related blood tests (thyroxine level) at the same visit.
- Reassess symptoms and adjust therapy based on test results; arrange follow-up appointment to review findings and plan.
